bibliography.title: Design Strategies for Anti-Freeze Electrolytes in Aqueous Energy Storage Devices at Low Temperatures

mechanism_relevant_findings: The decline in electrochemical performance of aqueous energy storage devices at low temperatures can be attributed to the freezing of the electrolyte, which leads to slow ion diffusion.
Deteriorated wettability results in restricted ion transport at the electrode-electrolyte interface.
The formation of regular hydrogen bond networks among water molecules is the primary cause for its high freezing point characteristics.
limitations: The review does not provide specific experimental data or numerical analysis.

relevance_judgement.reason: The paper discusses mechanisms affecting proton transport but lacks quantitative EIS analysis.
